title: Drug Concentration Math
sources: Critical Vector — Anesthesia Reference: Drug Concentration Math

changelog.change: Initial entry — percent-to-mg/mL rule, common local anaesthetic concentrations, and the epinephrine ratio-strength conversions.

summary: Percent concentration × 10 = mg/mL (1% = 10 mg/mL). Ratio strength is grams per total mL: 1:1000 = 1 g in 1000 mL = 1 mg/mL; each further 10-fold dilution divides the concentration by 10.

body.text: Multiply the percent by 10. A 1% solution is 1 g per 100 mL = 10 mg/mL.
1:X means 1 gram in X mL. Divide 1000 mg by X to get mg/mL.

rows: IV epinephrine in cardiac arrest (1 mg = 10 mL)
Infiltration with local anaesthetic (dental, some blocks)
Epinephrine added to local anaesthetic for vasoconstriction / test dose

body.text: Quick checks: an epinephrine 'push-dose' pressor is usually 10 mcg/mL — take 1 mL of the 1:10,000 arrest syringe (0.1 mg/mL) into 9 mL saline. A 1:200,000 test dose of 3 mL delivers 15 mcg of epinephrine (a rise in HR/BP suggests intravascular placement).

Local anaesthetic max doses are weight-based in mg — always convert the percent to mg/mL first. E.g. lidocaine with epinephrine max ~7 mg/kg: a 70 kg adult tolerates ~490 mg = ~24.5 mL of 2% (20 mg/mL). See the LAST reference for toxicity thresholds.
